headline: Bank manager booked in 1 crore fraud case
content: Times News NetworkLudhiana: Daresi police booked the manager of ICICI Bank’s Sunder Nagar branch for allegedly siphoning off Rs 1.41 crore from customers’ accounts.The FIR was lodged against accused bank manager Rahul Sharma on on the complaint of Tejpal Singh of Kakowal village.The complainant said that he, his father, wife, daughter and son have their accounts in ICICI bank’s Sunder Nagar branch, where the accused has been working as a manager for almost a decade now. Tejpal said that as he was an old customer, Sharma knew him well and would also provide him good facilities. Gradually, Sharma even befriended him and started visiting his house. Tejpal added that in 2014, he received a notice from the income tax department regarding some transactions in their bank accounts. When he went to the bank, Sharma allegedly took the notice from him and said he would send a reply to the I-T department on the bank's behalf. Thereafter, Tejpal never received any notice. However, in Jan 2024, he again received an I-T notice, after which he went to the bank. As Sharma was on leave that day, he inquired about the issue from other staff members. On checking the bank accounts, he was shocked to see multiple transactions, which his family and he never made.The victim alleged that the accused deposited money into their accounts several times and withdrew it by forging their signatures. The accused siphoned off about Rs 1.41 crore from the accounts.Sub-inspector Harpreet Singh, SHO at Daresi police station, said the police have registered a case under sections 408 (criminal breach of trust), 420 (cheating) and 120 B (criminal conspiracy) of the IPC after an inquiry was conducted by the ADCP- investigation.
